lipsync.loop_mode_note: Carried over unchanged, but it no longer triggers: the corrected driving base is 99.62 s, longer than every call, so LatentSync never loops it. That is what removes the repeating blink pattern and the reversed blinks structurally.

split.method: re-encoded at the cut (a stream copy snaps to the nearest keyframe and would desync the remuxed audio); trimmed UP to a whole 25 fps frame so video >= audio

audio.note: LatentSync's returned audio (aac 16 kHz) is DISCARDED; the locked 24 kHz -24.5 LUFS master is remuxed with -c:a copy (locked rule 4). Verified: the master's decoded PCM is an exact prefix of the mp4's, the only difference being 47 samples (1.96 ms) of mp3 decoder padding at the tail.

revision.reason: Blink cadence. The 5.04 s motion base contains four blinks (47.6/min); pingpong-looping it delivered 48.9 blinks/min on a 10.0 s repeat, with half of them played backwards on the reverse leg. Corrected by re-ordering the APPROVED base frames into a 99.62 s driving base - 13.3 blinks/min, irregular, none reversed.
